concepts.name: Sample space and outcomes
concepts.summary: List all possible outcomes of a simple experiment such as a coin toss, die roll or card draw.

concepts.name: Events as outcome subsets
concepts.summary: Describe an event as a subset of the sample space and identify which outcomes belong to it.

concepts.name: Standard dice, coins and cards
concepts.summary: Recall the structure of a fair coin, six-sided die and 52-card deck (suits, ranks, face cards).

concepts.name: Classical probability formula
concepts.summary: Compute probability as favourable outcomes divided by total equally likely outcomes and explain why.

concepts.name: Probability scale and complement
concepts.summary: Interpret probabilities between 0 and 1 and use P(not A) = 1 - P(A).

concepts.name: Relative frequency interpretation
concepts.summary: Explain probability as the long-run proportion of times an event occurs in repeated trials.

misconceptions.text: After several heads in a row, tails is more likely on the next toss.
Any two outcomes of an experiment are equally likely, so the probability of a sum of 7 with two dice equals that of a sum of 2.
A probability of 1/2 means the event will happen exactly once in every two trials.

concepts.name: Addition rule for events
concepts.summary: Apply P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A and B), including the mutually exclusive case.

concepts.name: Multiplication rule for independent events
concepts.summary: Compute the probability of joint events by multiplying when events are independent, and check independence.

concepts.name: Tree diagrams
concepts.summary: Build and read tree diagrams to find probabilities of sequences of events, with or without replacement.

concepts.name: Counting principle and factorials
concepts.summary: Count outcomes of multi-step procedures by multiplying choices and use factorial notation.

concepts.name: Permutations versus combinations
concepts.summary: Choose between and calculate nPr and nCr according to whether order matters.

concepts.name: Two-way tables and Venn diagrams
concepts.summary: Organise overlapping events in Venn diagrams and two-way tables to read off probabilities.

concepts.name: Conditional probability definition
concepts.summary: Calculate P(A|B) = P(A and B)/P(B) from tables and trees and interpret it as a restricted sample space.

misconceptions.text: Mutually exclusive events are the same as independent events.
Combinations and permutations of the same selection give the same count, so order never matters.
The probability of having a disease given a positive test is the same as the probability of a positive test given the disease, so the two can be swapped.

concepts.name: Law of total probability
concepts.summary: Split an event over a partition of the sample space and sum weighted conditional probabilities.

concepts.name: Bayes' theorem
concepts.summary: Use Bayes' theorem to reverse conditional probabilities, as in diagnostic test problems, using total probability for the denominator.

concepts.name: Testing independence of events
concepts.summary: Test whether events are independent by comparing joint and product probabilities, and distinguish pairwise from mutual independence.

concepts.name: Random variables and distributions
concepts.summary: Define a discrete random variable and build and validate its probability distribution table.

concepts.name: Expected value and variance
concepts.summary: Compute E(X), Var(X) and standard deviation from a distribution and interpret them.

concepts.name: Binomial distribution
concepts.summary: Recognise binomial settings and compute probabilities, mean np and variance np(1-p).

concepts.name: Counting with repetition and restrictions
concepts.summary: Analyse counting problems with repeated items, restrictions or complements to choose a valid method.

misconceptions.text: A positive result on a 99% accurate test means a 99% chance of having the condition, regardless of how rare it is.
The expected value must be a value the random variable can actually take.
Any experiment with two outcomes is binomial, even if trials are dependent or the probability changes.

concepts.name: Poisson distribution
concepts.summary: Model counts of events in a fixed interval with rate lambda, and decide when Poisson fits better than binomial.

concepts.name: Continuous random variables and density
concepts.summary: Interpret probability as area under a density, and relate density to the cumulative distribution function.

concepts.name: Normal distribution and z-scores
concepts.summary: Standardise values and use the normal curve and its 68-95-99.7 behaviour to find probabilities and quantiles.

concepts.name: Approximating binomial distributions
concepts.summary: Judge when normal or Poisson approximations to the binomial are valid and apply continuity correction.

concepts.name: Linearity of expectation
concepts.summary: Use indicator variables and linearity of expectation, even for dependent variables, to solve counting-expectation problems.

concepts.name: Variance of sums and covariance
concepts.summary: Analyse how variance of a sum depends on independence and covariance, and how scaling transforms mean and variance.

concepts.name: Law of large numbers
concepts.summary: Explain how sample averages converge to the expected value and what this does and does not guarantee.

misconceptions.text: The law of large numbers means deviations from expected results must be 'corrected' by opposite results.
For a continuous variable, P(X = x) is the height of the density curve at x.
The variance of a sum is always the sum of the variances.

concepts.name: Central limit theorem reasoning
concepts.summary: Evaluate when the CLT justifies normal approximations for sums and means and assess its limits with heavy tails or small samples.

concepts.name: Modelling choice among distributions
concepts.summary: Critique and select a distribution (binomial, Poisson, normal, other) for a real situation by testing its assumptions.

concepts.name: Bayesian updating with priors
concepts.summary: Evaluate how prior choice and sequential evidence shape posterior beliefs, including base-rate neglect.

concepts.name: Probability paradoxes and fallacies
concepts.summary: Resolve counterintuitive problems by rigorous conditional reasoning and identify the flawed intuition behind each.

concepts.name: Probability bounds and inequalities
concepts.summary: Apply and compare Markov and Chebyshev bounds to guarantee tail probabilities without knowing the full distribution.

concepts.name: Simulation and Monte Carlo design
concepts.summary: Design simulations to estimate probabilities and expectations, and judge their error from sample size.

concepts.name: Constructing probability models
concepts.summary: Create a probability model for a novel problem, such as a random walk or queue, by defining sample space, variables and assumptions and deriving results.

misconceptions.text: The central limit theorem says that any dataset becomes normally distributed once it is large enough.
In the Monty Hall problem, the two remaining doors are equally likely so switching makes no difference.
A very small probability of the evidence given innocence equals a very small probability of innocence given the evidence.
